newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch shares end lacklustre day up on Wall St open.
newsitem.headline: Dutch shares end lacklustre day up on Wall St open.

text.p: Dutch shares swung higher in late trade to end a lacklustre session in positive territory after Wall Street's firmer opening kindled fresh enthusiasm.
The AEX index of Dutch blue chip shares finished 3.78 points higher at 989.03 after spending most of the day a couple of points down on Thursday's 985.25 close.
Dealers said volumes had been markedly lower than in previous days, with private investors staying sidelined and most institutional activity on the sell side.
Buying interest was turning to cyclical stocks as other sectors started to look over-priced they added.
A string of cyclical stocks will publish first-half figures next week, and analysts' earnings prognoses are broadly positive, they added.
A major beneficiary of the new-found enthusiasm for cyclicals was chemical and drugs group Akzo Nobel which added 5.90 guilders to 299.00 in late trade.

Dealers said the stock had been helped by reports of lower dioxide prices hitting Imperial Chemical Industries' earnings. This pointed to improved margins for Akzo's coatings business when the company reports second-quarter earnings next Thursday, several noted.
Sector rival DSM, also set to report next week, finished 0.20 guilders higher at 228.00 after spending most of the day in negative territory.
Dealers said the relative lack of sales volume, a single foreign seller had driven down the stock price, which at one point hit a low of 221.00.
Other cyclicals also performed well, with steelmaker Hoogovens gaining five guilders to 126.50 and paper maker KNP BT adding 2.40 guilders to 47.40.
Philips Electronics built modestly on Thursday's 9.20 guilder gain, adding 0.80 to 172.10.
